text:
maya: heads-up — saw a weird 99th percentile latency jump on long-context runs around 11:03. looks like KV pager activity spiked and coincided with token-serving stalls. attaching quick dump.

ben: hmm, which pager metric spiked? `kv.pager.evictions_per_s` or `kv.reclaim_ms`?

maya: `kv.pager.evictions_per_s` went from ~40 -> 600 for a few seconds. also saw `kv.swap_io_wait_ms` climb. no recent code deploys to pager. applied to a large-batch chat workload with ~120k token histories.

profiler-bot: automated profile attached: top stacks during spike:
```
1) kv::page_out_loop  34%
2) runtime::serve_token 22%
3) async_io::block_on 18%
```

carla: interesting — could be fragmentation + our eviction heuristic failing under extreme working set churn. did we hit the high watermark that forces active compaction?

maya: yes exact watermark hit at 11:03:07 — `kv.memory_used_bytes` crossed `kv.memory_high_watermark_bytes`. compaction started, but compaction tasks queued behind heavy I/O and blocked token pipelines.

dave: are we still using strict LRU with global list? that can cause expensive updates if entries are large. FIFO avoids pointer chasing but can evict useful prefixes.

erin: quick note: the model's KV entry sizes are non-uniform here (early layers small, last layers huge). LRU updates touch the tail of a linked list which is hot. seems like contention on the LRU lock.

ben: can you paste the lock contention sample?

maya: paste: `mutex:kv_lru::hold_ms` spikes from 0.2 -> 12 ms under load.

carla: that matches. two failure modes: 1) LRU lock contention increasing latency, 2) FIFO evictions causing cache-miss storms when model reuses recent prefixes. we need a middle ground.

maya: idea I tossed in local testing: per-shard LRU with approximate timestamps (age buckets) + async background eviction to avoid inline compaction during serving. preliminary run reduced 99th by ~40% but increased aggregate evictions.

dave: can we add a soft watermark that flips to aggressive batching of evictions instead of compaction? like when memory > soft_wm start async reclaim until below soft_wm, only when crossing hard_wm block requests.

erin: also worth exploring reuse heuristics: track reuse_count per entry and prefer evicting entries with reuse_count==0 older than X. cheap to maintain as byte counter increments.

profiler-bot: quick experiment log from maya's run:
```
config: per-shard-age-buckets=true, soft_wm_pct=75, hard_wm_pct=92
result: p99 down 38%, p50 unchanged, evictions up 1.8x
issue: occasional background compaction IO spikes still visible
```

ben: good. let's schedule a controlled canary with that config + IO rate limit for compactor to smooth spikes. target: keep `kv.swap_io_wait_ms` < 2ms and p99 < baseline*1.1.

maya: filed a short runbook in the ticket for on-call: if we see similar p99 spike, flip `kv.compactor_io_limit` to 10MB/s and enable `per_shard_age_buckets`.

carla: one more: add a correctness test that replays long-context sequences and asserts no token-order regressions after eviction/paging. we had a subtle race earlier where async eviction touched active KV windows.

maya: noted. I'll add an integration test that runs 200k token replay with intentional eviction pressure and compares outputs.

dave: cooldown: :thumbsup: and assign owners: maya (investigate tests+canary), ben (canary infra + metrics), carla (algorithm follow-up), erin (KV telemetry).

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: #1840-kv-pager-canary — scheduled small fleet canary at 17:00 UTC.

maya: wrapping up — thanks all. will post results after the 17:00 run. :rocket:
